title: KV cache contention and attention tail-latency analysis
content: Summary:\nThis note captures an exploratory profiling run to investigate intermittent tail-latency spikes we observe when serving long-context requests (8k+ tokens) on the FlashAttention path. Hypothesis: interactions between KV cache management and fused attention kernels cause cache thrashing and kernel-launch contention, producing p95/p99 latency tails. The document details test harness, commands, microbench results, traces (summary), reproducible steps, and recommended next steps.
content_2:
Why this matters:
- Customer impact: interactive chat and streaming apps see occasional 200-800ms extra token latency on p99, violating some SLOs for enterprise customers on Dedicated Tier.
- Surface area: affects FlashAttention (fused kernels) primarily, but paged-attention path shows different behavior that looks more stable at high seq lengths.
- Goal: narrow root cause, propose short-term mitigations and a longer-term fix in runtime scheduling or kernel selection heuristics.
content_3:
Test harness and environment:
- Hardware: p4d.24xlarge-like node (8x A100 40GB equiv).
- CUDA: 12.1, cuDNN: 9.0, driver: 535.xx.
- Serving runtime branch: profile/kv-atten-2025 (commit: a1b2c3d).
- Model: 13B decoder-only (dense), seq_len tests: 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384.
- Workload: synthetic prefix + streaming continuation; 256 concurrent sessions ramped to 1024 active inflight tokens.
- Modes compared: FlashAttention (fused ops enabled), FlashAttention with fused ops disabled, PagedAttention (paged kv cache), and baseline naive attention kernel (reference).
- Profilers used: NVIDIA Nsight Systems (nsys), nvtx markers in runtime, CUPTI sampling for kernel times, and Linux perf for CPU-side mutex contention.
content_4:
Key commands (repro):
- run load generator: python infra/loadgen.py --model 13B --seq 8192 --clients 512 --tokens_per_client 2048 --streaming
- profile subset: nsys profile --sample=cpu --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=kv-8192-flash.nsight ./bin/serve --config profile.yaml
- collect kernel times: python tools/parse_nsys.py kv-8192-flash.nsight > kv-8192-flash.summary
- toggle fused ops: set env FUSED_OPS=0 and restart runtime
- enable paged kv: set CONFIG_KV_PAGED=1

Note: loadgen ensures token inter-arrival distribution approximates real chat bursts (We used a Weibull shape=1.5 to model burstiness).
content_5:
Measurements (selected):
- Baseline naive kernel (seq 8192, 512 clients): mean token latency: 18.6ms, p95: 45ms, p99: 92ms
- FlashAttention (fused ops ON): mean 11.4ms, p95: 48ms, p99: 210ms
- FlashAttention (fused ops OFF): mean 12.3ms, p95: 36ms, p99: 98ms
- PagedAttention (seq 8192): mean 13.8ms, p95: 34ms, p99: 85ms

Interpretation: fused ops enabled gives best mean latency but worst p99. Disabling fused ops increases mean slightly but collapses the tail dramatically. PagedAttention is more stable at high sequence lengths, suggesting KV cache layout and memory residency matter for peaks.
content_6:
Trace and hotspot summary:
- Nsight timelines show periodic kernel-launch storms when many sessions cross a certain prefix length threshold simultaneously. The storm aligns with KV cache refills and a set of large fused attention kernels executing back-to-back across multiple SMs.
- Kernel durations for the fused path have high variance: some invocations 6-8ms, others 50-120ms. The long ones correlate with CUDA page faults and device memory async copies triggered by paged KV hits.
- CPU side: we observed threads contending on a single cache-manager mutex (serializing KV eviction and copy-on-write). perf shows ~35% cycles in that lock during spikes.
- GPU occupancy is high during fused kernels; when a long kernel executes it appears to stall subsequent smaller kernels, amplifying tail latency.
content_7:
Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache eviction + synchronous copy path: when many sessions need to materialize large KV pages concurrently, runtime takes a global lock and issues big device->host->device transfers that block kernel launches and produce tail spikes.
2) Fused kernel launch overhead + variable input shapes: fused kernels choose specialized tiling that performs poorly when KV pages are not resident, causing slow paths to be taken.
3) PCIe/NVLink saturation on host-managed memory when paged mode is enabled and many shards fault in pages at once.
4) Scheduler co-location: runtime schedules mixed seq-length requests on same GPU stream, and fused kernels with long duration preempt smaller token-generation kernels.
content_8:
Micro-experiments performed:
A) Single-session ramp: replayed 1 session with gradually increasing prefix length while profiling. Result: p99 for that session remained stable until a threshold; crossing threshold caused local kernel time jumps (indicates shape-dependent path selection).
B) Staggered start experiment: start 512 sessions staggered by 10ms vs start-all-at-once. Stagger reduced p99 by ~40%.
C) Lock shaving: replaced global KV mutex with per-shard fine-grained locks in a test binary. p99 reduced by ~55% under same load.
D) Force-fuse-off: disable fused kernels at runtime (env var) and observe tails disappear but mean latency rises ~8-12%.
content_9:
Actionable short-term mitigations (can be implemented in days-weeks):
- Stagger session starts in load-balancer / token admission control: add jitter to session warmup to avoid synchronized faults.
- Disable global KV lock: fall back to per-shard locks or an event-queue for background page materialization to avoid blocking token generation threads.
- Kernel fallback threshold: add a heuristic to prefer non-fused attention for requests when KV residency score is low. This gives safer p99 while keeping mean benefits for warm requests.
- Backpressure policy: when background copy queue length exceeds X, throttle new sessions or route to paged-attention nodes.
content_10:
Longer-term changes (quarter-scale):
- Async page materialization: move KV page fetches to a dedicated IO thread pool with prefetching based on prefix heuristics. Avoid synchronous host<->device copies during the token-critical path.
- Improve fused kernel shapes: add fallback kernels for the case where KV pages are not resident or memory strides are unfriendly. Consider runtime autotune per-device for tiling.
- Scheduler improvements: give fused long-running kernels lower priority on CUDA streams or use multiple CUDA streams with stream priorities (if supported) to avoid preemption of short token kernels.
- Telemetry: augment per-token tracing to emit KV-residency score, lock wait times, and memory-migration counts to correlate with customer SLOs.
content_11:
Proposed immediate experiments (next 2 weeks):
- Implement per-shard locks in a staging branch and run the same load profile to verify p99 improvement at scale. (Owner: Alexei)
- Add residency heuristic to runtime: when < 80% KV pages resident, choose paged attention or non-fused kernels. Run A/B against baseline. (Owner: Priya)
- Implement and test staggered session admission in loadgen and in the production LB shim to measure real-world impact. (Owner: Ethan)
- Run direct NVLink saturation tests to measure host-managed memory behavior under mass page-faulting. (Owner: María)

Each experiment should publish the nsys timeline, parsed kernel summaries, and a short note with observed p50/p95/p99 and resource utilization.
content_12:
Open questions / risks:
- Is there a reproducible customer query pattern that triggers this (not just synthetic)? Need to mine prod traces to find correlated events (owners: SRE + CS).
- Are there hardware/driver-level behaviors (page faulting) we can’t reasonably mitigate at runtime? If so, we may need to recommend reserved capacity or different instance types for enterprise customers.
- Disabling fused ops improves p99 but increases cost per token. Need cost/benefit analysis for defaulting to fused-off under some conditions.
content_13:
Logging and dashboards to add:
- KV residency heatmap per-node (percent resident over time)
- Lock-wait time series per-runtime shard
- Kernel variance alert: when kernel duration variance > threshold for 5m raise incident
- Model-route SLO dashboard: correlate token p99 with KV residency and host copy queue length

Notes: these dashboards will help SRE and solutions-engineering decide if customer impact is due to workload or infra.
content_14:
Appendix - sample nsys findings (excerpt):
- Top kernels by time (fused path): fused_attn_forward_v2: avg 7.1ms, stddev 14.3ms, max 118ms
- Memory operations: host_to_device_async (page materialize): 0.9GB/s peak during storms
- CPU hot functions: kv_manager::evict_and_copy (34% CPU during spike), runtime::dispatch_token (12% blocked waiting on lock)

Raw experiment artifacts stored: s3://redwood-profiled/kvcache/2025-02-14/ (nsys .qdrep + summary).
content_15: Decision log (proposal):\n- Short-term: merge per-shard-lock change into canary (10% traffic) and enable kernel fallback heuristic. Monitor p99. If tails reduce by >40% without >10% mean regression, roll to 100%.\n- If mitigations insufficient: schedule deeper work to redesign KV materialization pipeline and prioritize scheduler changes in Q2 roadmap.
